# Gospel of Thomas, Saying 65 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Nag Hammadi Codex II, p. 48 | **Source Image:** source-texts/coptic/GTH_065_page_001.jpg

---

## Saying 65

**1** He said: "A good man had a vineyard. He leased it to some tenant farmers so that they would work it and he would receive the produce from them.

**2** He sent his servant so that the farmers would give him the produce of the vineyard. They seized his servant, beat him, and nearly killed him. The servant returned and told his master.

**3** The master said: 'Perhaps they did not know him.' He sent another servant. The farmers beat that one as well.

**4** Then the master sent his son and said: 'Perhaps they will show respect for my son.' Because the farmers knew that he was the heir to the vineyard, they seized him and killed him.

**5** Whoever has ears, let him hear."

---

**Consensus Notes (SOPHIA):**

**"Good man"** — *agathos* preserved as the simplest rendering; LOGOS's "creditable" is interpretively loaded and not required by the Coptic.

**Text:** Thomas's version of the Wicked Tenants parable is notable for: (1) adding *agathos* to describe the owner, (2) the double rationalization of the owner ("perhaps they did not know him"), (3) no divine retribution ending, (4) no Isaiah 5 vineyard frame.

**Synoptic Parallels:** Mark 12:1-12; Matt 21:33-46; Luke 20:9-19. This parable has been central in debates about whether Thomas preserves an independent, earlier version (Patterson, Crossan) or is a simplification of Synoptic sources.

**Theological Note:** The absence of allegorical commentary lets the parable breathe as narrative. Thomas does not explain who the owner, servants, or son represent.
